high.title: Prabowo Moves to Crack Down on State-Owned Enterprises, Calls Them 'Sources of Corruption'
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto publicly declared that state-owned enterprises (SOEs/BUMN) have long been hotbeds of corruption and pledged to bring them under stricter control. This statement, made at the National Cooperative Day celebration, signals a potential major governance overhaul across Indonesia's extensive SOE sector. Investors in BUMN-listed companies should monitor for upcoming regulatory or structural changes that could affect operations and profitability.

high.title: Prabowo Decrees All Subsidized Goods Must Be Distributed Through Red-White Village Cooperatives
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has made a binding decision that all government-subsidized goods must be distributed exclusively through the Koperasi Desa/Kelurahan Merah Putih (Red-White Village Cooperatives). This policy aims to ensure subsidies reach their intended recipients and prevent misuse. The cooperatives will be developed into integrated village economic service centers offering grocery stores, savings and loan services, and village pharmacies, representing a significant restructuring of Indonesia's subsidy distribution system.

high.title: Prabowo Approves Special Fuel Price of Rp 15,000/Liter for Fishermen
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has approved a special subsidized diesel fuel price of Rp 15,000 per liter for fishing vessel operators with boat sizes between 30 to 200 gross tons. This comes after non-subsidized fuel prices spiked to Rp 21,300 per liter, significantly burdening the fishing industry. The policy represents a major government intervention in the energy sector with direct implications for fisheries-related businesses and fuel subsidy expenditure.

high.title: S&P Predicts Rupiah to Return to Rp 17,700/USD Level
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings has affirmed Indonesia's credit rating at BBB/A-2 with a stable outlook, while projecting the rupiah to strengthen to Rp 17,700/USD in 2026 and further to Rp 17,500/USD in 2027. This is notable as the rupiah currently trades weaker at Rp 18,109/USD as of Monday's close. The rating affirmation and positive currency outlook are significant signals for foreign investors and holders of Indonesian assets.

high.title: JCI Surges Strongly, Returns to 6,000 Level
high.summary: Indonesia's composite stock index (JCI/IHSG) closed up 1.92% at 6,037.84, recovering from an opening level of 5,934.71. Trading volume reached 26.30 billion shares with a total transaction value of Rp 12.13 trillion. This marks a significant recovery back above the psychologically important 6,000 level, signaling renewed investor confidence.

high.title: Volkswagen Giant Reportedly in Crisis, Planning to Lay Off Up to 100,000 Employees
high.summary: German automaker Volkswagen is planning an additional 50,000 layoffs on top of a previous 50,000 cuts, bringing the total potential workforce reduction to 100,000 employees globally, including subsidiaries Porsche and Audi. The decision follows a 20% profit loss driven by billions in tariff costs and intense competition in China. This signals deepening stress in the global automotive sector, which may impact Indonesian auto-related stocks and suppliers.

high.title: S&P Global Ratings Affirms Indonesia's Credit Rating at BBB/A-2 with Stable Outlook
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings has reaffirmed Indonesia's sovereign credit rating at BBB (long-term) and A-2 (short-term) with a Stable outlook, keeping the country firmly in investment grade territory. The rating is supported by strong economic growth prospects, prudent macroeconomic policy, and relatively low external and government debt. Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto highlighted this as a positive signal for investors, noting Indonesia maintained ~5% growth and fiscal deficit below 3% of GDP amid global uncertainty.

high.title: S&P Projects Rupiah to Strengthen Back to Rp 17,700/USD
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings projects the Indonesian rupiah will strengthen to Rp 17,700/USD in 2026 and further to Rp 17,500/USD in 2027, indicating an optimistic outlook for the currency. This is notable as the rupiah currently closed weaker at Rp 18,109/USD, suggesting significant potential upside according to S&P's forecast. This projection is tied to S&P's broader affirmation of Indonesia's BBB/A-2 credit rating and reflects confidence in Indonesia's macroeconomic fundamentals.

high.title: President Prabowo Approves Special Fuel Price of Rp 15,000/Liter for Fishing Vessel Operators
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has approved a special subsidized diesel fuel price of Rp 15,000 per liter for fishing vessel operators with boats sized 30 to 200 gross tons, down significantly from the non-subsidized price of Rp 21,300/liter. This policy decision was made during a cabinet economic meeting at the President's residence in Hambalang, Bogor. The move has direct implications for state energy company Pertamina's fuel pricing structure and the broader fisheries sector economy.

high.title: JCI Surges Strongly, Returns to the 6,000 Level
high.summary: Indonesia's composite index (JCI) closed up 1.92% at 6,037.84 on Monday, July 13, recovering from an opening level of 5,934.71. Trading volume reached 26.30 billion shares with a transaction value of IDR 12.13 trillion, signaling a strong return of market activity. This recovery back above the psychologically important 6,000 level is a key positive signal for Indonesian equity investors.

high.title: S&P Rating Announcement Seen as Fresh Boost for JCI
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings affirmed Indonesia's long-term debt rating at BBB and short-term at A-2, maintaining a stable outlook, which MNC Sekuritas credited as a key driver behind the JCI's 1.92% rally to 6,037.84 on July 13. The maintained investment-grade rating restores short-term investor confidence in Indonesian capital markets. This decision is significant as it signals international confidence in Indonesia's fiscal and economic stability amid global uncertainty.

high.title: Revealed: The Culprit Behind the US Dollar Briefly Pushing Rupiah to IDR 18,000
high.summary: The Indonesian Rupiah briefly touched IDR 18,000 per US dollar on July 6, driven by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials that pushed the DXY dollar index to a one-year high. Bank Indonesia noted that the Fed maintained its funds rate at 3.5–3.75% in June but market participants anticipate further rate hikes ahead, adding pressure on emerging market currencies including the Rupiah. This significant Rupiah weakness raises concerns for import costs, inflation, and foreign debt servicing for Indonesian businesses.

medium.title: Prabowo Warns of Foreign Entities That Come to Trade but End Up 'Robbing' Indonesia's Wealth
medium.summary: President Prabowo used his speech at the National Cooperative Day event to criticize foreign parties who enter Indonesia under the guise of trade but ultimately exploit the country's natural resources and wealth. The remarks suggest a more nationalistic and protectionist tone in the administration's economic policy outlook. Foreign investors and multinational companies operating in Indonesia should take note of potential shifts in regulatory sentiment toward foreign business activities.

medium.title: Garuda Indonesia Changes Free Baggage Policy to Piece Concept Starting September 1
medium.summary: State-owned carrier Garuda Indonesia will shift its free baggage allowance system from a weight-based concept to a piece-based concept effective September 1, 2026, applying to all tickets purchased from that date onward. This policy change could affect passenger costs and competitiveness relative to other carriers, and may have implications for Garuda's ancillary revenue streams. Investors in Garuda Indonesia (GIAA) should assess whether this shift improves yield management and overall financial performance.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Rp 15,000 Per Gram Over the Past Week
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices declined by Rp 15,000 per gram over the trading week of July 6–11, 2026, closing at Rp 2,655,000 per gram after opening the week at Rp 2,670,000. The week saw mostly downward movement with brief recoveries on Friday and Saturday. This price trend is relevant for retail investors and traders tracking precious metals as a safe-haven asset in Indonesia.

medium.title: KKP Adds Patrol Vessels and Expands Batam Dock to Combat Illegal Fishing
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (KKP) is strengthening its maritime surveillance infrastructure with 10 new Class I patrol vessels and an expanded base dock in Batam, targeting the North Natuna Sea fishing management zone. The expansion will bring the total patrol fleet to 44 units, aimed at curbing Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated (IUU) Fishing. This investment signals increased government spending on maritime security and could positively impact the domestic fisheries sector by better protecting national marine resources.

medium.title: Garuda Indonesia Changes Free Baggage Policy Starting September 1: Here's How It Works
medium.summary: State-owned airline PT Garuda Indonesia (Persero) Tbk will shift its free baggage policy from a weight-based concept to a piece-based concept for all tickets issued from September 1, 2026. Under the new policy, Economy Class passengers will receive up to 23 kg per piece (up from 20 kg), while Business and First Class allowances increase to 32 kg from 30 kg. This change in service policy could affect passenger satisfaction and operational costs for Garuda, which is listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange (IDX: GIAA).

medium.title: OJK Issues New Pension Fund Regulation Allowing Lump-Sum Benefit Payments
medium.summary: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) has issued a new ruling (KEP-54/D.05/2026) allowing pension fund benefits — including severance pay components — to be paid out in a lump sum, following two Constitutional Court decisions in 2025. The regulation provides legal certainty for pension fund participants and aims to protect the stability of the pension fund industry. This change could have material implications for corporate liabilities and pension fund management across Indonesian businesses.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Rp 15,000 Per Gram Over the Past Week
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices declined by Rp 15,000 per gram over the trading week of July 6–11, 2026, closing at Rp 2,655,000 per gram after opening at Rp 2,670,000. The week saw consecutive daily drops before a partial recovery on Friday and Saturday. This weekly movement is relevant for retail investors and traders tracking gold as an alternative asset class in Indonesia.

medium.title: Garuda Indonesia Changes Free Baggage Policy to Piece Concept Starting September 1
medium.summary: State-owned airline Garuda Indonesia will shift its free baggage allowance calculation from a weight-based concept to a piece-based concept effective September 1, 2026, applicable to all tickets purchased or issued from that date. This policy change affects all passengers on Garuda-operated flights and could impact customer satisfaction and competitive positioning relative to other airlines. Investors in Garuda Indonesia (GIAA) should monitor the effect on passenger volume and revenue.

medium.title: IDX Head Responds to Public Linking JCI Movement to President Prabowo's Speech
medium.summary: Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) President Director Jeffrey Hendrik stated that political conditions currently have minimal impact on JCI movements, noting that the correlation between politics and investment decisions has significantly decreased compared to the 1980s. His comments come amid widespread social media discussion linking JCI fluctuations to President Prabowo Subianto's public speeches. The clarification aims to reassure investors that market movements are driven by fundamentals rather than political sentiment.

medium.title: Details of Discussion Between Finance Minister Purbaya and Said Iqbal on Eliminating JHT (Retirement Fund) Tax
medium.summary: Presidential Special Advisor for Labor Affairs Said Iqbal met with Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa to discuss a proposal to eliminate taxes on Jaminan Hari Tua (JHT) retirement fund withdrawals, arguing social savings programs should not be taxed like commercial accounts. Said Iqbal is pushing for a 0% tax rate and removal of progressive taxation on JHT withdrawals, which can currently reach up to 30% for workers who have experienced multiple layoffs. If approved, this policy change would benefit millions of Indonesian workers and could affect government fiscal revenue projections.

medium.title: Microsoft Lays Off 4,800 Employees
medium.summary: Microsoft is cutting approximately 4,800 employees, representing 2.1% of its global workforce, to reduce costs in the artificial intelligence era. The Xbox division is the hardest hit, losing roughly one-fifth of its staff. This reflects the broader global tech industry trend of restructuring around AI, which Indonesian tech investors and companies should monitor closely.

medium.title: Ministry of Finance Responds to S&P Report: International Community Still Trusts Indonesia
medium.summary: The Ministry of Finance, through Director General of Financial Sector Stability Herman Saheruddin, welcomed S&P's affirmation as evidence of continued international trust in Indonesia's fiscal discipline and economic resilience. The Ministry emphasized Indonesia's commitment to maintaining fiscal discipline in line with President Prabowo's directives. This reinforces the government's narrative of economic stability amid global volatility.

medium.title: OJK Issues New Pension Fund Regulation Allowing Lump-Sum Benefit Payments
medium.summary: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) has issued a new decision (KEP-54/D.05/2026) allowing pension fund benefits — including those derived from severance pay, service recognition payments, and compensation rights — to be paid out in a lump sum to participants, spouses, or dependents. The regulation follows two Constitutional Court rulings and aims to provide legal certainty for the implementation of those decisions while safeguarding the stability of the pension fund industry. This is relevant for companies managing employee pension funds and participants planning retirement withdrawals.

medium.title: IDX Opens the Door for BYD and Tencent to Enter Indonesia's Stock Exchange via Single Stock Futures
medium.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) is finalizing an agreement with Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEx) to allow major Chinese companies such as BYD and Tencent to be listed on Indonesia's market through Single Stock Futures (SSF) instruments rather than direct share listings. IDX President Director Jeffrey Hendrik confirmed the deal is in its final stages, which would significantly expand the range of investable assets available to Indonesian retail and institutional investors. This move could attract new investor interest and increase market depth and liquidity on the IDX.

medium.title: Netizens Link JCI Movements to President Prabowo's Speech — IDX CEO Responds
medium.summary: IDX President Director Jeffrey Hendrik downplayed viral social media claims linking JCI fluctuations to President Prabowo Subianto's public speeches, stating that the correlation between political activity and market movements has significantly diminished compared to the 1980s. He emphasized that investment decisions in Indonesia are increasingly driven by economic fundamentals rather than political events. This clarification is relevant for investors assessing the risk of political noise on Indonesian equity markets.
